body: Decision card v1 for Indraprastha Medical Corporation Ltd (Indraprastha Apollo Hospitals, Sarita Vihar). Rule output: size 0: blocked by Expected value vs hurdle (EV 1.39x anchored (raw 1.35x) vs hurdle 1.76x → below hurdle → size 0). Thesis: Method-test thesis: Indraprastha Medical (one ~700-bed Apollo-run hospital in Delhi) earns a ~50% ROIC partly because its land is leased from the Delhi government at Re 1/month in exchange for a free-treatment obligation it has under-delivered (7-10% vs 33% IPD / 40% OPD per GNCTD). The lease expired 31-Jul-2023 and the JV agreement 10-Mar-2018; GNCTD told the Supreme Court on 27-Jan-2026 that renewal would be 'contrary to public interest'. The 5-year outcome is a legal/political binary layered on a good operating business, not an operating-earnings call. Variant view: Market: at Rs 356 the stock trades at 17.0x trailing P/E and 9.8x EV/EBITDA net of Rs 521 cr cash, against hospital peers at 33-59x (median 48x) - a ~65% discount that IS the lease risk. A simple two-state read (going concern at ~30x = ~Rs 630/share vs handover value ~Rs 60-90/share) puts the price-implied probability of a workable renewal at roughly 50% [EST]. Our view: no claimable mispricing - we have no edge on a Supreme Court / Delhi-government outcome, and the evidence we found leans NEGATIVE relative to how the company presents it: (1) the FY26 annual report, the Q2 FY27 results notes and the MD&A do not mention that the lease and JV agreement have expired or the January affidavit (only a 3-Feb-2026 board-outcome paragraph 'noted' it), while the contingent-liability note says the company 'has remained compliant with the applicable requirements under the lease'; (2) the Delhi government (26% holder, a promoter) did not vote its shares at the 24-Sep-2026 AGM (promoter votes polled 21.44m of 46.75m) and has not nominated its 3 directors including the Chairman; (3) the MD's term ended 4-Nov-2026 with no successor announced; (4) ROIC is flattered by the land subsidy, so any renewal on market or stricter-EWS terms compresses margins. Positive offsets: Rs 521 cr net cash (16% of market cap, Rs 57/share), no debt, steady ARPP-led growth (+11% TTM revenue, 18% OPM), and courts and governments usually prefer stricter terms to closing a 700-bed hospital. What would prove us wrong: a 30-year renewal on terms close to IMCL's own ask (10% IPD / 25% OPD incl. medicines) with no retrospective claim. Departure from the outside view: our raw P(blow-up) 20% and P(<=0.5x) 26% are ABOVE the class base rates (15% / 11%) because of a specific, dated legal threat; anchored at w=0.3 (evidence note). Checked by paper calls thesis:paper-call:INDRAMEDCO:*. Open soft flags: 6. P(≥3x) 7% vs base 21%; P(≤0.5x) 26% vs base 11.3%; EV 5-yr multiple 1.35x vs hurdle 1.76x. Review 2027-02-15.
